blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: PC — Program Counter; next instruction address.
throughput — Work completed per unit time.

blocks.title: Fetch the instruction
blocks.text: PC identifies address 72, which MAR sends to memory. MDR transfers its contents to CIR.

blocks.title: Differentiate performance improvements
blocks.text: Cores can execute independent work; cache helps when needed data/instructions are present.

blocks.title: Explain limits
blocks.text: Branching, shared memory bandwidth, serial dependencies and software constrain real speedup.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict
blocks.text: Copy PC=40 into MAR to select the instruction location.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain
blocks.text: Instruction contents travel via MDR to CIR, while sequential PC advances to 41.

blocks.title: Predict
blocks.text: Each available core receives a separate independent job.

blocks.text: Ideal duration is the longer job, five minutes; serial execution would take eight.
